noStates: Policy definitions have no status field that the program writes or tests, so they have no states in the usual sense. What the code does keep is their condition on disk, and the download changes it. Before a download, the destination folder holds no definitions or older ones. A successful download replaces them, file by file, with the Microsoft package version: any existing file of the same name is deleted and the new one moved in. Nothing is rolled back if a move fails halfway. The folder is then left with a mix of old and new definition files, and the failure is only reported as a message naming the step that failed. Failure also leaves a scratch folder under the user's local application data behind, holding the partly unpacked package and possibly the downloaded installer file. That folder is removed only when every step succeeds. When the user is an administrator, the download also rewrites the destination folder's owner and permissions. After a successful download the user may choose to load the folder, and the program then saves it as the saved setting for the definitions source folder. Loading itself never changes a definition: a file either loads or is reported as a load error at that moment, and nothing about it is stored.
